pathways.climate_pressure: Recurrent climate disasters damaging infrastructure and safe-water access.
pathways.documented_impact: Assistance needs overlap with violence-related service deprivation.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Armed actors, insecurity and mobility restrictions constrain assessment, monitoring and sustained humanitarian operations.
pathways.possible_consequence: Climate-disaster assistance may be harder to sustain within the constrained multisector response.
alternative_explanations: Road damage, isolation, institutional capacity and response resources also constrain access.
pathways.uncertainty: Conditional synthesis of an official summary; no named climate-adaptation project suspension or measured climate-response effect is demonstrated.
resilience_factors: Existing humanitarian capacity is acknowledged, but the source judges it insufficient for needs.
pathways.compact_statement: Insecurity constrains multisector response where climate disasters add needs; climate-specific operational effects remain an inference.

gaps: OCHA's official summary supports a conditional reverse operational mechanism, but no named climate-adaptation project suspension or quantified climate-response effect was established.
Nonviolent social protest and policy reversal remain institutional context; no climate-to-criminal-violence pathway is inferred.

FEWS NET's May 2026 outlook through December 2026 remains explicitly dated, conditional and unverified against later outcomes; national food availability is distinct from household safe access and affordability.

executive_assessment.text: Local vulnerability includes coastal flood and erosion records, Amazon/coastal poverty sensitivity, and named provinces facing overlapping protection and service needs.

A conditional reverse mechanism connects documented insecurity-related access barriers to response in territories also affected by climate disasters. It does not establish that a named adaptation project stopped.

Basin-specific agricultural recommendations are distinguished from delivery. Dated food-security forecasts emphasize violence-related purchasing-power loss and compounding weather, without attributing violence to climate.
